title: Site comparison preserves the support localization boundary
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:V=T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $F$ be an ordinary sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on the small etale site, viewed in degree zero in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $F_p=\nu_T^*F$; identify $j^{-1}F_p$ with $\nu_V^*(j^{-1}F)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

Let $c_T^q$ and $c_V^q$ be the degree-$q$ global-section comparison maps induced by the derived adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Let $c_C^q$ be the degree-$q$ map of the canonical support comparison $c^C_{T,F}$ of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison], with supported cohomology defined by the kernel-of-restriction right derived functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q$ and $\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q$ be the connecting maps of the two support long exact sequences [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], using the same cochain/snake-boundary convention in the two topologies. Then the triples $(c_C^q,c_T^q,c_V^q)$ form a morphism between these long exact sequences. In particular, for every $q\geq0$,
$$
c_C^{q+1}\circ\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q
=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q\circ c_V^q:
H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},j^{-1}F)\longrightarrow
H^{q+1}_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F_p).
$$
All squares, including the restriction and forgetting-supports squares, commute without an additional sign. These maps and squares are natural in $A_T$-linear morphisms of $F$; in particular all comparison maps and connecting maps are $A$-linear. No constructibility or freeness assumption is imposed on $F$.

source.place: Tag 09XP, label section-cohomology-support, displayed injective restriction sequence, distinguished triangle and its long exact sequence. Compatibility with the specified etale/pro-etale adjunction-unit comparison is an agent-formulated refinement of this construction; the tag alone does not assert this comparison.

proof.text: Work in a common universe in which both sites are small. Their ordinary $A$-module categories are Grothendieck abelian by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] to choose a bounded-below injective module resolution $F_p\to J^\bullet$. The module adjunction is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and its inverse image is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Consequently [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] shows that $I^\bullet=\nu_{T,*}J^\bullet$ is bounded below and termwise injective on the etale site. This uses preservation of injectives by direct image, rather than an assertion that inverse image preserves injectives.

source.place: Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives; derived.tex Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist; sites-cohomology.tex Section 07A5; injectives.tex Tag 079H.

proof.text: Let $a:F\to I^\bullet$ be the ordinary comparison unit followed by $\nu_{T,*}(F_p\to J^\bullet)$. By the injective computation of right derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], $I^\bullet$ represents $R\nu_{T,*}F_p$, and by [lem-pur-comparison-unit-injective-model], applied to $M=F$ in degree zero and the resolution $F_p\to J^\bullet$, $a$ represents the derived adjunction unit under this identification. That unit is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], with no constructibility hypothesis. Thus $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism and is a specified etale injective resolution of $F$. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] gives $I^r(T)=J^r(T)$ and $I^r(V)=J^r(V)$, with identical restriction maps and differentials. Taking kernels gives $\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{et}},I^\bullet)=\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},J^\bullet)$, using [def-pur-support-cohomology].

source.place: Tags 099V, lemma-relative-comparison (2), and 09B1, lemma-compare-derived (2); derived.tex Tag 05TI, lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived.

proof.text: For completeness the degreewise surjectivity needed for localization also holds for module injectives. For an injective module sheaf $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-injective-presheaf] makes its underlying module presheaf injective. For the monomorphism $j:V\to T$, the map of free presheaves $A[h_V]\to A[h_T]$ is injective: on each object its basis map is the injection $\operatorname{Hom}(-,V)\to\operatorname{Hom}(-,T)$. By the definition of injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions], restriction of Hom into $E$ is surjective. The free-presheaf Yoneda formula [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] identifies this with $E(T)\to E(V)$. Therefore in either topology the three complexes $\ker(E^\bullet(T)\to E^\bullet(V))$, $E^\bullet(T)$, $E^\bullet(V)$ form a degreewise short exact sequence when $E^\bullet$ is $I^\bullet$ or $J^\bullet$. The kernel and both arrows respect the $A$-actions.

source.place: Tag 03FB, lemma-injective-module-injective-presheaf; module version of the monomorphism restriction argument of Tag 093X.

proof.text: The support complex in each row computes the right-derived kernel functor of [def-pur-support-cohomology], with the ordinary module-coefficient interpretation of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]; the middle complex computes global sections. The restrictions $I^\bullet|_V$ and $J^\bullet|_V$ are injective resolutions on their respective sites by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. Thus the last complexes compute cohomology on $V$. These are precisely the injective localization models for the long exact sequences of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. The finiteness of $A$ makes every coefficient sheaf torsion, and the hypotheses of the pro-etale clause hold. No finiteness of the modules of sections is needed.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open, and Section 03FA, cohomology of modules.

proof.text: The equalities in Step 2 identify the two short exact sequences of Step 3 term by term, including their inclusions and restriction arrows. They therefore give a morphism of short exact cochain complexes. Its support component represents the canonical supported comparison of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]: first apply the etale derived support functor to the unit $F\to R\nu_{T,*}F_p$, represented by the augmentation $a$, and then use the kernel identity of Step 2. In the specified resolution $a:F\to I^\bullet$, the first operation is represented by the identity on the support complex of $I^\bullet$. The middle component is the global comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] by the same unit computation. On $V$ it is the global comparison for $j^{-1}F$: restriction of $a$ is the adjunction unit there, since the direct-image restrictions are the same maps $J(T)\to J(V)$. The coefficient identification is the canonical $j^{-1}F_p\cong\nu_V^*(j^{-1}F)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Thus the three cohomology maps are exactly the specified $c_C^q,c_T^q,c_V^q$, rather than unspecified isomorphisms of their groups.

source.place: Tags 099V, lemma-relative-comparison, 099W, lemma-compare-cohomology, and 09B1, lemma-compare-derived; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09XP, kernel localization model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] to this morphism of short exact complexes. The result is a morphism of the full long exact sequences, with $c_C^{q+1}\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q c_V^q$. To see the sign explicitly, a cocycle on $V$ is lifted to a cochain on $T$, its differential lies in the support kernel, and the class of this differential is the connecting image. The termwise identifications send the chosen lift and its differential to the same cochains in the other row. Both boundaries therefore give the same class, with no negation. Naturality of the comparisons in [lem-pur-support-site-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], and coefficient functoriality of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], give naturality of all these squares in $F$. All complexes and their arrows are $A$-linear, so their induced cohomology and connecting maps are $A$-linear as well.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain; Tag 08N7, lemma-snake-natural. The explicit lift-and-differentiate computation uses the same boundary convention in both rows.

The mathematics is correct. Step 1 pushes a pro-etale injective resolution forward with nu_*, which keeps it injective because nu^* is exact; this does not rely on inverse image preserving injectives. Step 2 holds because nu_* is evaluation at the same object, so the two complexes have identical sections and identical support kernels. Step 3 shows restriction to V is surjective for module injectives, via the free-presheaf monomorphism and Yoneda; this is elementary and correctly marked. Step 4: restriction preserves injectives because an open immersion is etale and weakly etale, and the torsion hypothesis holds because n*A=0 for n the characteristic of A. Step 5 identifies the three components with the unit-induced comparisons c_C, c_T and c_V.
